title: Briarwake Development Roadmap
purpose: A dependency and evidence map for Briarwake, an Unreal Engine 5 native C++ MMORPG. This documentation owns gameplay contracts and progress; evanmcpheron/BriarwakeUnreal owns the newly versioned native bootstrap. Completion depends on scoped executed evidence rather than planning or historical engine results.

BW-001 and BW-001-T08 are Complete for the recorded macOS ARM64 Development matrix: actual Editor/Game/source-Server builds, nonempty client/console-Server packages, visible independent client launch, three-tick headless checks, missing/invalid configuration rejection, decoded-Pak inspection and clean build/runtime failure controls. Exact logs, hashes, commands, revisions and limitations are retained in validation/tickets/BW-001-T08/final/review.json. BW-002 and all seven of its tickets are Complete for reviewed boundaries and content admission. Two fresh native seven-test aggregates at game 5dd6e53e945aecc204cf59df88b162de3c87b85d each pass 3,584 content assertions, including 797 complete economic graph checks; all 25 default FULL stages, independent failure/recovery controls and Game/source-Server package isolation pass. Current five-criterion review and exact source/canonical/build identities are retained in validation/tickets/BW-002-T06/parent-review.json. Historical T01-T05 execution evidence remains retained at its original revisions. Current 2026-10-22 review: BW-003 and all five tickets are Complete after the T05 four-criterion review at game 03f16be061e5f6f1991d1fa86f1d560cda3ab90b, with native source SHA-256 fac818a71e8f8790d51d8c1161d2ff1885899c908ca3054c1a791b91fc276f72 still matching inspected game main f90e86a741df3dc778af61d79944289baffbd7af. Retained validation/tickets/BW-003-T05/review.json records 46 default FULL stages, 66 Python regressions and two 242-assertion fixture aggregates. BW-003 leaves Dependency-ready; BW-097/BW-095 join BW-018/BW-004/BW-005/BW-006 as Not Started and Dependency-ready. BW-097 now has six unexecuted camera-reference tickets; planning does not advance its status. No production economic handler, connected Steam session, production gameplay fixture system, persistence, capacity, Shipping or other-platform certification is implied.
reading_guide: Each epic is one coherent, demonstrable capability with a permanent BW identifier, scope, hard prerequisites, acceptance criteria and required evidence. Phases group integration objectives derived from the dependency graph; they do not require every independent branch to wait for the previous phase.

Navigate from the dashboard to a phase index, then open an individual epic page. Every epic has direct links to its prerequisites, downstream work, recommended sequence neighbors and numbered acceptance criteria. Existing dashboard and phase epic bookmarks lead to the same canonical epic page.

Hard dependencies must be Complete before the dependent epic can be completed or meaningfully verified. Recommended predecessors improve risk reduction or integration efficiency without becoming technical gates. Direct dependencies are preferred; prerequisite closure supplies inherited requirements.

The displayed sequence is a reasoned engineering recommendation, not an immutable technical fact. Numerical IDs do not imply priority. Reorder an epic only after checking its dependencies and integration gates; keep its ID and anchor stable.

An epic reaches Complete only when every acceptance criterion has passing, revision-specific runtime/content/operational evidence and its hard prerequisites are Complete. Criteria define observable behavior rather than internal methods. Failure scenarios are part of completion. Status does not advance automatically when a document or fixture specification is written.

Milestone requirements include their transitive hard prerequisites. Explicit integration/certification epics test connected behavior on compatible builds. Phase completion means every member epic is Complete; it does not replace those integrated proofs.

Foundations certify the state families in their tested package. An epic introducing another family must extend the applicable recipient-view, reconstruction, security and operational checks before admitting it. This never certifies a future family in advance; full-roster and release certification still cover their entire declared scope.

The selected presentation is low-resolution 3D pixel art inspired by David Holland. Camera/readability and art-production work have their own evidence gates; continuous planar/floor simulation remains authoritative. Historical references to eight sprite directions now mean compatible preview headings, not a required spritesheet pipeline.

The owner selected evanmcpheron/BriarwakeUnreal as the separate native C++ implementation repository. Reverify its Git root, task branch and pinned toolchain before execution. The supplied MultiplayerSessions Steam plugin has baseline compilation/widget checks; authoritative replication, connected sessions and provider capabilities remain unverified. Ticket planning does not establish implemented gameplay.

distinctions.label: Documented requirement
distinctions.meaning: An explicit gameplay or integrity rule in the feature reference; preserve it regardless of the recommended schedule.

distinctions.label: Technical constraint
distinctions.meaning: A real limitation such as recipient-safe value replication or one active owner; a tool capability is not evidence that the game meets it.

distinctions.label: Hard dependency
distinctions.meaning: A capability needed to complete or meaningfully verify another epic, represented by an explicit ID edge.

distinctions.label: Recommended ordering
distinctions.meaning: A judgment about risk, testability, integration or maintenance; independent work may move earlier.

distinctions.label: Assumption
distinctions.meaning: An unverified working expectation, recorded with a resolution gate rather than treated as a fact.

distinctions.label: Open decision
distinctions.meaning: A future implementation/configuration/content choice that current evidence cannot responsibly settle.

analysis_method: First inventory capabilities across feature prose, 501 canonical structures, class/specification catalogs, professions, content-readiness flags and existing audits. Separate simulation, durable ownership, recipient views and content-production responsibilities. Establish prerequisites from observable behavior and failure cases, then identify parallel branches and small experiments that expose costly assumptions. Compare alternatives on rework, security, testability, operational recovery and unnecessary complexity. Only then topologically order the capabilities and group them into the phases below. A final reverse review traces every documented family to the full-game gate and challenges unnecessary edges.

phases.title: 1. Executable boundaries and risk probes
phases.objective: Establish reproducible runtime evidence, a versioned content-production route and durable ownership independently of combat. Verify orthographic camera framing and initial visual readability alongside headless development.
phases.completion_condition: The durable retry/crash probe is executed against a real candidate store. The author/import route produces a reproducible reviewed package and rejects invalid content. A reproducible 3D reference scene verifies camera projection, target readability and initial visual/performance settings.

phases.title: 2. First authoritative multiplayer interaction
phases.objective: Connect protected clients, move and resolve one visible action, then measure the small integrated workload.
phases.completion_condition: The integrated two-client action and early load probe pass; no durable player journey is claimed.

phases.title: 3. Recoverable combat and personal state
phases.objective: Combine reusable encounter rules with durable identity, progression, equipment and reconnect behavior.
phases.completion_condition: The initial combat/character reconstruction proof passes; later mechanics add their own reconstruction cases.

phases.title: 4. First complete persistent player journey
phases.objective: Deliver an initial supported beginner and role slice with security, support and restore gates for external persistent testing.
phases.completion_condition: The representative beginner/role playtests use a common compatible build, and provider security plus actual restore evidence permit external persistent play. The starter slice integrates the reviewed 3D art workflow and camera.

phases.title: 5. Bounded mechanics and safe world evolution
phases.objective: Prove the remaining state families, local isolation, simple distributed handoff and safe versioned updates.
phases.completion_condition: Family fixtures and initial transfer/update proofs pass; the comprehensive advanced-state regression is BW-089, not inferred here. The combined-mechanic multiplayer/workload probe passes before broad kit certification.

phases.title: 6. Complete roster and beginner certification
phases.objective: Bind the intended class/specification/talent inventory and certify all legal beginner characters.
phases.completion_condition: Every cohort and early legal character journey is certified; isolated cohort passes do not replace the all-roster beginner gate.

phases.title: 7. Player exchanges and profession services
phases.objective: Deliver shared economic and social branches, useful item operations and complete six-band profession content.
phases.completion_condition: Transactions and profession content pass their own contention and failure evidence; full economic relevance is evaluated in BW-072.

phases.title: 8. Full progression, cooperative and competitive experiences
phases.objective: Complete level-cap journeys, group/PvP content, advanced recovery, balance and presentation evidence.
phases.completion_condition: All-roster, progression, economic, group/PvP and usability certification pass; BW-092 separately verifies their release-candidate integration. Complete environment art and accessibility evidence are included.

phases.title: 9. Measured capacity and production acceptance
phases.objective: Verify full-game integration under an approved workload, rehearse incidents and make the evidence-based release decision.
phases.completion_condition: No required epic, unresolved release-blocking decision or missing mandatory evidence remains; controlled release acceptance is recorded.

epics.title: Reproducible client and headless project
epics.objective: Prepare and create the first native C++ Unreal Engine 5 project with reproducible client and dedicated-server execution from zero.
epics.scope: Install and verify the required Unreal Engine 5 editor, native C++ compiler/toolchain and build prerequisites; select a tested engine revision; create a new C++ project and its separate game repository; configure client and dedicated-server build targets, versioned settings and foundational smoke tests. No existing project, servers or plugins are assumed. The owner selected evanmcpheron/BriarwakeUnreal for the implementation and requested inclusion of its supplied engineering docs and MultiplayerSessions Steam plugin. Bootstrap uses the canonical ServerConfiguration contract; Steam account/session behavior and gameplay remain outside this baseline.
acceptance_criteria: On a documented clean machine, the developer can install the required engine and native C++ toolchain, create a fresh C++ Unreal project in an explicitly chosen separate repository, pin the tested engine revision, and produce launchable client and dedicated-server targets using recorded build, cook and package steps.
The compiled dedicated server starts without rendering or a local player and reports its executable, engine, rules and content revisions; the client can be launched separately.
Missing required configuration fails with an actionable diagnostic; credentials are absent from distributed client artifacts.
A clean automated run distinguishes build failure from an executed passing or failing runtime check.
epics.completion_evidence: Versioned native project/repository, pinned engine and toolchain identities, clean C++ client/server build and package logs, exact artifact hashes, actual client launch and headless-server smoke, configuration rejection, credential inspection and distinct automated failure controls.
epics.ordering_rationale: The owner-selected separate native C++ repository and pinned macOS ARM64 Development baseline have executed build, packaging, independent client/headless-server launch, configuration rejection, decoded-Pak inspection and clean failure-control evidence. BW-001 completion does not establish connected Steam sessions, gameplay, persistence, Shipping or other platforms.

epics.title: Orthographic camera and visual-readability proof
epics.objective: Verify a character-following camera that starts in an elevated angled orthographic view, smoothly scrolls into a close third-person perspective, and orbits the character on middle-mouse drag, while preserving readable 3D gameplay and world picking.
epics.scope: A reproducible Unreal Engine 5 native C++ 3D reference scene with an elevated, angled orthographic default camera; scroll-wheel zoom that lowers and tilts toward a close, behind-character third-person view; reverse zoom back to the original overview; and held middle-mouse drag to orbit the camera around the controlled character. Include representative character/environment assets, camera-to-world picking, independently scaled UI and baseline visual-performance checks. This is camera presentation only; full art production and any changes to authoritative movement or aim are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible Unreal Engine 5 native C++ reference scene records the tested engine/toolchain, default and close-view camera settings, scroll and middle-mouse input mappings, target hardware and supported display settings; no previous game implementation is assumed.

At the default zoom, an angled top-down orthographic view follows the controlled character and keeps the playable floor, targets and independently scaled UI readable across supported window sizes and high-DPI displays. Scrolling inward moves toward a close, behind-character third-person perspective; scrolling outward returns to the elevated orthographic view with no abrupt camera jump or loss of focus.

Holding middle mouse and dragging horizontally orbits the camera around the controlled character; vertical dragging changes pitch within safe limits. Releasing middle mouse stops orbit. Stationary, following and diagonally moving tests confirm smooth yaw/pitch, continuous scroll transitions and stable character framing without rotating, moving or re-aiming the character through camera input.

Representative models, equipment and terrain are reviewed at elevated and third-person gameplay distances for consistent art proportions, legible silhouettes, clear target markers and hazards in bright and dark scenes.

Camera zoom, projection transition, orbit, resizing, occluding geometry, UI-captured pointer input and layered-floor views preserve valid world picking and ground-target previews. Hidden and cross-floor entities are never disclosed, and camera presentation never alters authoritative movement or aim.

Versioned reference scenes reproduce on declared target configurations; still/motion captures document both views, scroll/orbit behavior, readability and accessibility findings, CPU/GPU frame cost, memory and supported-quality decisions.
epics.completion_evidence: Versioned reference scene and camera/input/display settings, captured scroll transitions and middle-mouse orbit in both viewpoints, representative visual comparisons, world-picking/occlusion and readability tests, and measured performance. No finished game renderer or production asset library is implied. Explicit owner completion override, 2026-10-23: BW-097 and all six tickets are administratively Complete as requested. The failed reference cook and unexecuted rendered/performance QA remain preserved as actual historical results in BW-097-T06 setup; no new execution or measurements are claimed.

epics.completion_evidence: Headless geometry/movement fixtures with authoritative position and input traces.

epics.title: Derived attributes and bounded resources
epics.objective: Resolve numerical character state without requiring a complete class roster.
epics.scope: Attribute scaling, racial offsets, combat conversions, resource maxima and regeneration; specialized resource hooks are certified later.
acceptance_criteria: Published allocation/formula fixtures produce the documented derived values with the declared rounding and modifier order.
Resource gains, reservations and regeneration cannot exceed caps or produce negative available balances.
Healer fixtures use Mana plus a signature meter; class/race changes cannot silently alter documented eligibility or base reach.
Invalid resource kinds, caps and unsupported numerical content are rejected rather than given guessed defaults.
epics.completion_evidence: Executed numerical boundary fixtures and comparison to existing arithmetic examples.

epics.title: Entity lifecycle and recipient snapshots
epics.objective: Give clients a coherent view of entities they are allowed to observe.
epics.scope: Spawn/despawn, revisions, initial baselines, owner-private state and visible public value projections; broad interest scheduling is BW-013.
acceptance_criteria: Two clients agree on authoritative movement and entity identity after join, leave and re-entry.
A new observer receives current state rather than depending on an earlier event it never saw.
Stale or duplicate snapshots do not resurrect despawned entities or overwrite newer state.
Owner resources and private recovery state are absent from another client’s public snapshots; unavailable references fail safely.
epics.completion_evidence: Two-client lifecycle traces including late join and stale snapshot injection.
epics.ordering_rationale: Begin value projections with movement and identity. Add cast/status/projectile projections with their gameplay rules rather than designing a universal final replicator.

epics.title: Predicted movement and reconciliation
epics.objective: Keep local movement responsive while the server retains the final position.
epics.scope: Local movement prediction, acknowledged input reconciliation and remote interpolation; no predicted damage or unrestricted historical hit rewind.
acceptance_criteria: At 0, 50, 100, 150 and 250 ms RTT, correction converges to the server position without applying acknowledged input twice.
Jitter and 1–5% packet loss do not leave permanent remote motion divergence after state delivery resumes.
Collision corrections and ownership changes discard obsolete prediction history and cannot move a character through a wall.
Record correction magnitude/frequency and input response for each scenario, with an explicit review of understandable failure at 250 ms.

Render-camera alignment and visual interpolation do not quantize predicted or authoritative positions; slow tracking during correction and teleport/reset cases remain understandable in the selected low-resolution view.
epics.completion_evidence: Network-impairment runs with motion traces, correction metrics and reviewed recordings.
epics.ordering_rationale: Movement semantics must exist first. Prediction is proven before broad human testing, but does not block isolated combat or durable-state work.

epics.title: Target relations and legal spatial intent
epics.objective: Resolve eligible targets and aiming from authoritative information.
epics.scope: Target lock/cycling, friendly selection, line/cone/ground/self modes, reach, line of sight and floor rules; visual controls integrate in BW-028.
acceptance_criteria: Target cycling follows angular difference, distance and stable-ID ordering and excludes illegal hidden/dead/friendly/cross-floor candidates.
Every admitted targeting mode resolves the required intent fields and rejects unused or invalid target data.
Range, relation and geometry failures leave resources and cooldowns unchanged at acceptance.
Ground placement rejects protected, inaccessible and closed-door locations; faction/group relation changes are rechecked when required.
epics.completion_evidence: Target-policy fixtures over all supported modes, relations and geometry failures.

epics.title: Cast commitment and ability timing
epics.objective: Resolve one authoritative ability lifecycle with precise failure semantics.
epics.scope: Learned/build checks, reservations, GCD, cast/channel/instant timing, release revalidation and cooldown commitment; no full roster.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance verifies ability/build/equipment/life/control/target/resource permissions and reserves costs only for legal commands.
Interrupted pre-release casts release reservations, preserve the started GCD and do not consume the ability cooldown under release-commit.
Channels commit at start without refunds on cancellation; accepted instants commit cost and cooldown together.
Movement cancellation, target loss, late input and duplicate commands yield declared outcomes with no extra cast or resource spend.
epics.completion_evidence: Executed instant/cast/channel fixtures covering valid release, rejection, interrupt and duplicates.
epics.ordering_rationale: Timing and commitment rules precede expansion of effects and their replicated outcomes; animation never determines authoritative release.

epics.title: Damage healing and absorb resolution
epics.objective: Resolve effective combat results using documented numerical and accounting rules.
epics.scope: Primary effects, mitigation, criticals, healing, shields and bounded modifier order; recurring statuses and complex proc graphs follow separately. Bounded damage transfer uses the same effective-result accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Identical seeded contexts yield the documented modifier order, rounding and effective damage/healing/absorbed amounts.
Overkill and overhealing are recorded without increasing effective output, threat or reward contribution.
Support attribution sums only to the actual support increment under ordered marginal accounting and never adds damage again.
Resource/cooldown commitment and root action identity survive a rejected or duplicate result without extra outcomes.
Redirected damage obeys its cap, receives no second mitigation and cannot redirect recursively; an immune protector leaves damage on the original recipient.
epics.completion_evidence: Numerical execution fixtures including caps, shields and multi-source support attribution.

epics.title: Interest privacy and bounded state traffic
epics.objective: Keep disclosure correct as relevance and entity counts change.
epics.scope: Floor/instance/spatial interest, relevant hazards, explicit authorization removal, projection redaction and independent traffic priorities. Initial verification covers the implemented package; later state producers extend this disclosure contract.
acceptance_criteria: Hidden and cross-floor entities are absent from unauthorized snapshots, targeting queries and public correlation identifiers; client presentation and selection cannot reconstruct or reveal excluded entities.

For each currently implemented cast/status/effect state kind, interest entry restores current state without historical event replay; authorization loss removes or redacts it. Each later state-producing epic must pass these same projection checks before admission.
A hazard that can affect a recipient remains represented while unrelated cosmetic updates may be limited.
A recorded crowded synthetic scene demonstrates finite relevant sets, queue bounds and measured traffic; reliable chat-like traffic does not stall replaceable movement.
Tracking/reveal returns only authorized markers within declared bounds and cannot discover a hidden player or extend visibility through client camera zoom.
epics.completion_evidence: Packet inspection and visibility-boundary fixtures plus a documented synthetic-load trace.
epics.ordering_rationale: Privacy is a correctness boundary from the first integration. Final spatial tuning and launch capacity remain measurement-driven later work.

epics.title: Action controls and legible combat feedback
epics.objective: Expose enough accessible interaction to test actual gameplay decisions early.
epics.scope: Rebindable movement/target/cast input, action bar, HUD, queue/cancel, telegraphs, status/resource/cast/rejection feedback and presentation hooks; final asset production is separate. Projected world picking, independent UI composition and occluder-aware cues integrate with the active render view; placeholder art can serve the first technical proof.
acceptance_criteria: A player can target, preview/confirm/cancel ground intent, queue one eligible action within the documented window and see rejection reasons.
HUD/action bars show authoritative resources, GCD/cast/cooldown and target state; predicted feedback corrects after rejection.
Friendly-frame targeting has precedence and actionable hazards remain distinguishable without relying only on color.
Keyboard bindings, text/UI scale and reduced visual effects can be exercised independently of world display settings; model poses and camera presentation never determine aim, collision or release.

Pointer ground previews and selection map through actual viewport scaling, letterbox offsets and camera projection to the intended server floor/position; UI capture and invalid/occluded geometry have deterministic rejection/cancel behavior.
epics.completion_evidence: Keyboard/controller-if-supported interaction recordings and accessibility checklist with executed correction/rejection cases.
epics.ordering_rationale: Interaction and feedback belong beside the first technical slice so human tests can reveal control and latency problems; polished art remains later work.

epics.title: First authoritative multiplayer action proof
epics.objective: Demonstrate the smallest integrated movement-and-action loop before a full game journey.
epics.scope: Two test clients, one controlled target, authoritative direct action and visible rejection; temporary non-economic state is sufficient.
acceptance_criteria: Two clients move, select an eligible target and observe the same accepted cast and resulting health change from one authoritative action.
A forged hit, position or private-state request fails without changing authoritative state or revealing hidden data.
A late observer receives current health/cast state and packet loss followed by a baseline leaves neither client permanently stale.
The run records action latency, tick/traffic observations and a clear client failure reason; it claims no persistent economy or complete beginner experience.
epics.completion_evidence: An executed two-client scenario with correlated server/client traces and captured feedback.
epics.ordering_rationale: This narrow proof reduces the cost of discovering an incompatible command/simulation/projection boundary. A full offline combat kernel or full database product is not a prerequisite.

epics.title: Representative early simulation and bandwidth probe
epics.objective: Expose architectural bottlenecks using the first integrated multiplayer workload before broad content production.
epics.scope: Movement, direct actions, join/leave bursts and current entity counts on a declared test machine. This produces measurements and follow-up decisions, not a realm-capacity promise.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable workload drives moving clients and implemented actions, includes burst joins/departures, and records client count, content/rules versions, hardware and measurement duration.

Reports retain tick median/tail percentiles, queue depth, memory, bytes per client, rejection/duplicate counts and recovery behavior rather than connection counts alone. Record the actual client render configuration and frame timings separately so rendering cost is not mistaken for a server or bandwidth limit.
Latency runs include 0/50/100/150/250 ms RTT plus declared jitter, snapshot reordering and 1–5% loss; failures and rejected inputs remain visible.
The report identifies measured constraints and bounded next changes, explicitly distinguishes prototype rates from achieved capacity and records unresolved budgets before further scale claims.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: reproducible workload/configuration, raw measurements and a reviewed bottleneck report tied to the tested build, with reruns for any claimed improvement.
epics.ordering_rationale: A small integrated probe can invalidate expensive assumptions early; it should not wait for full professions, raids or the complete roster. It does not justify premature seamless worlds or microservices.

epics.title: Status lifecycle control and trigger bounds
epics.objective: Apply persistent combat effects without stacking or recursive event exploits.
epics.scope: Refresh/tick rules, cleanses, control/DR, stealth/immunity projections and bounded trigger attribution; summon objects are separate.
acceptance_criteria: DoT/HoT refresh preserves the next tick and 30% carry cap; shield and strongest-category rules prevent additive refresh exploits.
Cleanse selects one legal effect in documented priority; no eligible effect means no accepted cost or cooldown.

PvP duration caps, shared diminishing history, rolling allowances and boss immunity obey documented rules; rated control-break uses its shared 120-second cooldown and declared two-second category immunity.
Trigger depth/child bounds, proc exclusions and no-reflect/redirect/echo recursion hold; hidden status sources remain redacted.
Death/logout/transfer cleanup policies compose and preserve surviving expiry/tick/budget as declared.

Two-client late join, interest re-entry and authorization-loss tests reconstruct current status/tick state without a missing earlier event, while public status allowlists and hidden-source redaction remain enforced.
epics.completion_evidence: Executed status edge fixtures, control histories, event traces and filtered projection captures.

epics.title: Projectile and ground-effect execution
epics.objective: Resolve traveling and spatial effects independently of target-acquisition method.
epics.scope: Swept collision, hit budgets, lifetimes, homing/straight/piercing semantics, ground placement/ticks and relevant visual state.
acceptance_criteria: Fast projectiles cannot skip thin solid walls, closed doors or floor boundaries; piercing actor hits never imply wall penetration.
Homing impact rechecks relation/existence, straight attacks retain aim and repeated hits obey finite target budgets.
Ground effects enforce placement, tick timing, overlap/target caps and current hostile/friendly relations.

Committed attacks that hit a wall do not refund costs; actual damage/healing uses the shared resolver. Joining or re-entering interest receives the currently relevant hazard, schedule and expiry through independently authorized owner/public views.
epics.completion_evidence: Geometry/collision and ground-tick fixtures with two-client hazard snapshots.

epics.title: NPC engagement threat and reset
epics.objective: Make a bounded authored opponent engage, select actions and reset safely.
epics.scope: Finite NPC state/ability conditions, same-floor navigation, threat, leash and encounter-owned hazards; authored dungeon content is later.
acceptance_criteria: NPC behavior traverses idle, engaged, leashing and dead with legal finite priority scheduling and bounded navigation.
Effective damage, healing and consumed shields generate documented threat; taunt cannot engage a distant unengaged boss or affect players.
Aggro changes at the documented melee/ranged thresholds and scripted targets return to normal threat afterward.
Leashing clears encounter threat/hazards, restores home state and grants no reward or consumable refund; death emits one completion identity.
epics.completion_evidence: Executed threat, navigation, leash and reset fixtures with event histories.

epics.title: Death revival and solo recovery
epics.objective: Provide safe defeat and recovery without resetting committed obligations.
epics.scope: Atomic death cleanup, legal recovery destinations, food/rest baseline and encounter-shared revival charges; repair settlement connects in BW-026.
acceptance_criteria: Zero health stops casts, invalidates pet commands, settles outstanding damage obligations and marks death once.
Ordinary death deletes no items, levels or talent points; recovery cannot restore spent consumables or reset cooldown debt.
Out-of-combat revival follows documented duration/resources, and encounter charge budgets reset only on a genuine reset/completion.
Solo characters can recover without a required profession; illegal revival states or destinations fail with a visible reason.
epics.completion_evidence: Death/revival/reset fixtures, including repeat death messages and simultaneous revival requests.

epics.title: Account admission and exclusive character sessions
epics.objective: Bind real account authentication to revocable character authority.
epics.scope: Trusted opaque login/recovery adapter, transport protection, session expiry/revocation, single-owner epochs and permission checks; support workflows expand later.
acceptance_criteria: Only a verified unexpired scoped trusted proof admits an economic character; one-use proofs cannot be replayed.
A second connection cannot operate the same character concurrently and stale sessions/epochs cannot issue successful actions or grants.
Expiry, restriction, logout and recovery revoke the appropriate credentials and return actionable client states.
Missing lifetime/rate/payload settings disable affected endpoints; credentials and provider secrets are absent from client logs and artifacts.
epics.completion_evidence: Account-adapter integration and adversarial admission/session tests, including simultaneous login and revocation.
epics.ordering_rationale: Real identity precedes durable characters and shared assets; a restricted authenticated test session was sufficient for the earlier technical slice.

epics.title: Atomic character creation and selection
epics.objective: Create a legal durable character through the documented preview-and-review flow.
epics.scope: Faction/race/class eligibility, appearance choices, Unicode naming, account-scoped creation receipt, selection and safe initial entry.
acceptance_criteria: The preview/review/selection flow preserves compatible choices, exposes unavailable classes with reasons and retains the draft after failure; appearance/equipment presentation agrees with in-world resources, with eight heading presets supported without requiring spritesheets.
All eleven races and twelve faction-race selections obey class restrictions; Humans have identical racial attributes on both sides.
Naming fixtures cover documented normalization, grammar, realm-wide cross-faction uniqueness and retained reservations under a pinned Unicode revision.
Concurrent creates claim a name and starting records atomically; retry returns the same character and invalid appearance choices cannot enter.
epics.completion_evidence: Creation UI review and naming/eligibility/atomicity integration runs over the legal catalog.

epics.title: Inventory wallet and guaranteed delivery
epics.objective: Make personal assets durable and recoverable under contention and full bags.
epics.scope: Container placement, stack/split/move/consume operations, currency ledger, asset binding and pending reward delivery; exchanges use this common boundary later.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent asset changes validate owner/container/item revisions and cannot duplicate, overfill or produce negative stacks/currency.
Bound, reserved or escrowed assets cannot be transferred through personal inventory operations.
Full bags produce a durable claimable delivery; retry, restart and expiry of a loot corpse never destroy an awarded item.
Every committed asset change has an attributable receipt/ledger entry and reconnect reads the same ownership and balance.
epics.completion_evidence: Inventory/wallet contention, restart and full-bag claim tests with reconciled ledgers.

epics.title: Equipment placement and derived loadouts
epics.objective: Apply legal item loadouts to authoritative combat state.
epics.scope: Equipment slots/proficiencies, bag-to-equipment ownership, adaptive item budgets, binding and comparison UI; repair/enhancement settlement is BW-026.
acceptance_criteria: Equip/unequip atomically changes item/container/slot revisions and cannot leave an item equipped and in a bag simultaneously.
Class armor/weapon restrictions and two-hand/off-hand rules reject illegal loadouts.
Slot weights, grade multiplier, adaptive primary and reserved enchant budget apply once and match published examples.
Replacing equipment updates authoritative derived stats and shows comparable gains/tradeoffs without adding hidden instrument/tool slots.
Weapon/auto-attack output respects the normalized single/dual-weapon budget; faster swings cannot multiply the declared on-hit proc rate budget.
epics.completion_evidence: Equipment concurrency/eligibility fixtures, item-budget comparisons and loadout UI capture.

epics.title: Experience unlocks and specialization selection
epics.objective: Persist the documented level and role progression independently of the full content roster.
epics.scope: XP thresholds, level cap, class unlock schedule, banked specialization points, role training and level-ten selection.
acceptance_criteria: Level 1 begins with zero points; every level-up from 2 through 60 awards exactly one class and one specialization point.
Pre-ten specialization points remain banked; level ten selection exposes nine earned specialization points without an extra graduation award.
Abilities unlock at their declared levels and role training supplies mandatory tank/healer services rather than optional talents.
Repeated XP/unlock operations and restart preserve one award and a coherent level/build revision; illegal or premature selections reject.
epics.completion_evidence: Threshold/award/restart fixtures and level-ten selection demonstration.

epics.title: Talent legality and atomic build application
epics.objective: Accept legal builds and apply their declared behavior as one versioned change.
epics.scope: Tree budgets/prerequisites/exclusivity, previews, respec restrictions, rollback/revalidation and safe-point application; exhaustive content binding is later. Named saved loadouts contain both allocations, selected specialization, action bars and equipment-set references.
acceptance_criteria: Both trees enforce rank, tier, prerequisite, exclusive-choice and 59-point constraints at every spendable level.
Client previews never authorize a build; stale or invalid submissions preserve the previous active build and points.

Accepted named loadouts atomically apply both tree allocations, specialization, action bars and validated owned equipment-set references after the three-second stationary application; stale, missing or illegal equipment references and combat/damage interruption preserve the previous loadout.
A content change requiring refunds/revalidation preserves stable IDs and restores a legal build rather than retaining obsolete effects.

Application obeys party/encounter/match restrictions, never increases absolute current health or restores missing resources/cooldowns/debt, and removes old summons/auras/invalid action entries atomically.
epics.completion_evidence: Positive and exclusion talent fixtures, stale build contention runs and a migration/refund scenario.
epics.ordering_rationale: Build application needs the equipment ownership/slot boundary as well as progression. A legal talent allocation cannot authorize a stale or foreign equipment-set reference.

epics.title: Participation credit and durable loot awards
epics.objective: Turn one legitimate encounter completion into one eligible durable reward.
epics.scope: Engagement snapshots, contribution, open-world claims, loot selection/claim-pass and personal reward delivery; skinning rights remain separate.
acceptance_criteria: Engagement membership/bounds plus effective damage, healing, prevention, tanking or support qualify credit; late joins and ineffective farming do not.
Encounter/creature-generation and recipient identity grant once across duplicate deaths, retry and restart.
Guaranteed/probability/weighted loot modes follow declared tables; shared claim/pass persists one shuffled order and never rerolls on delivery retry.
Full bags retain awarded delivery and corpse expiry cannot delete it; leash/reset awards nothing.
epics.completion_evidence: Credit edge cases and persisted loot/delivery concurrency runs with reconciled completion identities.

epics.title: Vendor repair and enhancement settlement
epics.objective: Support basic preparation and item upkeep through durable personal services.
epics.scope: Buy/sell, repair/durability, enhancement/upgrade eligibility and confirmation; crafting-service production and recrafting are separate.
acceptance_criteria: Vendor quotes use declared price/eligibility configuration and stale, forged or unaffordable purchases cannot alter assets.

Ordinary PvE death reduces equipped durability by five percentage points; zero durability removes combat benefits while preserving ownership and repairability, and rated PvP applies no durability loss.
Repair, legal upgrade and enhancement application commit payment/materials and item revision together or leave all unchanged.
Confirmation/comparison discloses output and costs; binding, reserved enhancement budgets and incompatible categories cannot be bypassed.
Repair quotes use the explicit NPC-purchase-value/missing-durability formula and configured minimum; undamaged equipment costs zero and missing price/coefficient configuration rejects the quote.

Admission of vendor values checks the current enabled recipe/conversion graph for guaranteed material, currency or progression loops; invalid or missing required prices cannot enable a route. Craft sellback stays below guaranteed NPC-purchased input cost.
epics.completion_evidence: Vendor and item-service atomicity fixtures plus durability and comparison UI demonstration.

epics.title: Reconnect checkpoints and conservative crash recovery
epics.objective: Restore a character without duplicating authority or clearing obligations.
epics.scope: Disconnect grace, clean logout, owner-private reconnect baselines, cooldown/status/debt checkpoints and documented unclean encounter reset.
acceptance_criteria: In-combat disconnect retains the configured grace behavior without invulnerability or new player/pet commands; reconnect claims the existing character.
Reconnect restores durable assets/build/progress and surviving cooldown, status and damage obligations without duplicate rewards.
Logout and crash recovery apply declared cleanup/reset policies, never inventing exact replay of uncheckpointed combat ticks.
Expired/stale sessions and simultaneous reconnects leave one authoritative owner; the public snapshot is filtered separately from owner-private restoration.
epics.completion_evidence: Injected disconnect/crash/reconnect fixtures at cast, status, reward and build boundaries with reconciled ownership.
epics.ordering_rationale: Recovery is proven before a complete persistent journey. Exact tick replay is not required by the documented conservative recovery policy.

epics.title: Scoped communication and player reporting
epics.objective: Provide bounded communication and abuse controls as soon as testers interact socially.
epics.scope: Local/private/party/raid/guild routing, rate/restriction checks, mute/block/report and moderation history; group/guild channels activate only with authoritative membership.
acceptance_criteria: Local/private messages obey authoritative visibility, recipient restrictions, mute/block and configured spam limits without revealing hidden players.
Group/guild routes require current authoritative membership when those systems are enabled; absent membership cannot be forged.
Reports preserve relevant context and authorized moderation actions/restrictions are auditable without exposing secrets.
Reconnect and duplicate messages cannot bypass restrictions; denied sending returns an understandable result.
epics.completion_evidence: Routing/privacy/rate-limit fixtures and an auditable report-to-restriction test.
epics.ordering_rationale: Core communication can proceed independently of combat. Full party/guild routing is integrated when those memberships exist.

epics.title: Reusable 3D asset and animation production workflow
epics.objective: Make consistent characters, equipment and starter scenery producible through a repeatable reviewed art workflow.
epics.scope: Source models/textures, rigs, attachments, animation/material conventions, render-resource packaging and a representative starter kit; gameplay records retain their canonical authority and full-roster production is certified in BW-074.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed source assets reimport reproducibly with stable presentation references, scale, pivots, foot anchors, material settings and finite resource budgets; missing/incompatible assets produce actionable findings before package publication.

A representative character, equipped weapon/armor, alternate appearance and combat form preserve attachment alignment and readable silhouettes across approved camera views; preview and in-world rendering use compatible assets and materials.
Locomotion, casts, impacts, interruption, death and form changes follow authoritative event/time samples after prediction/reconciliation; model animation never changes hit geometry or attack release.

A compact terrain/prop/foliage kit and approved palette/value/material examples demonstrate the selected style in the starter view, with low-quality and occlusion variants; contact/shadow treatment does not mask legal targets or hazards.

An accepted and rejected art edit demonstrate resource validation, reviewed diffs, retained prior output and declared source/license provenance; the art package references existing gameplay content without adding a competing gameplay schema.
epics.completion_evidence: Versioned source/imported asset package, import and rejection logs, art conventions, representative actor/equipment/form motion captures and starter-kit comparison scenes at tested settings.
epics.ordering_rationale: Establish reusable art production before the first complete starter journey; backend creation and isolated combat fixtures may use declared placeholder assets in parallel.

epics.title: Signature meters, marks and action sequences
epics.objective: Represent bounded gameplay state derived from successful actions rather than speculative client events.
epics.scope: Representative owner/target marks, charge/sequence/phase state and event-qualified generators; all-kit numerical bindings follow.
acceptance_criteria: Representative owner meters, target marks and ordered action families obey declared caps, expiry, generation and spending.
Rejected, cancelled, repeated, overhealing and ineligible self-owned actions cannot manufacture qualifying progress.
One root action cannot grant per-target resources unless the explicit contract permits it.
A released action consumes its selected marks/charges once and exposes the same canonical state to applicable tooltips/UI.
epics.completion_evidence: Future event-boundary and invalid-action fixtures covering Guard, target marks and a sequence/phase mechanic.
epics.ordering_rationale: Mandatory level-10 roles already need signature state. Prove a small family before the first role slice instead of postponing every secondary mechanic as late content.

epics.title: Maintained songs and bounded support
epics.objective: Make support measurable without stacking unlimited group amplification.
epics.scope: Song slots/replacement/finales, category caps, effect attribution and visible aggregate strength; no rhythm-input requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Two ordinary song slots are available under the defined policy; a permitted third divides the same aggregate budget.
Song replacement/overlap and finalization consume the declared state once and obey category caps.
Effective allied contribution is attributable for encounter credit; unused or self-recursive support cannot farm rewards.
Movement and latency do not introduce audio-timing requirements; UI exposes maintained slots and strength.
epics.completion_evidence: Future stacking/overlap/finale fixtures and group contribution traces with visible song state.

epics.title: Party and raid membership
epics.objective: Let players form persistent-authority groups and inspect the capabilities they bring.
epics.scope: Invitations, leadership, removal, encounter locks, party/raid frames and capability inspection; reward settlement remains BW-025.
acceptance_criteria: Only recipients accept pending unexpired invitations; retries return the same terminal membership result.
Unauthorized leadership changes, over-capacity acceptance and disruptive encounter-time membership changes reject.
Party and raid views agree with server membership and show missing role-service categories without requiring a named class.
Party/raid communication routes only to current authoritative members and obeys the same mute/block/report and rate restrictions as direct/local channels.
epics.completion_evidence: Future invitation-race and permission tests, plus a multiplayer membership and role-inspection demonstration.

epics.title: Representative five-player role encounter
epics.objective: Prove tanking, healing and damage cooperate in one readable server-owned encounter.
epics.scope: Warrior, Bard and Mage representative kits, mandatory level-10 role services, encounter telegraphs and one completed five-player test; full roster certification follows.
acceptance_criteria: One tank, one healer and three damage players complete the authored encounter using shared-faction providers.
Threat changes, effective healing, consumed prevention and interrupts produce the documented authoritative results.
Every selected tank and healer has its mandatory role kit without optional talent purchases.
A wipe clears encounter-owned state while preserving player cooldowns, debt, consumed items and committed rewards.

The same encounter exercises a tank-facing cone, an interruptible cast, recoverable group damage, a moving hazard and a short priority-target phase with the documented readable setup; completion and wipe evidence cover their combined interaction.
epics.completion_evidence: Future recorded multiplayer run, role-service matrix and reset/failure fixture results tied to content revisions.
epics.ordering_rationale: An integrated role slice exposes threat, support and recovery errors before large catalogs multiply them; it does not require every specialization.

epics.title: Measured build and specialization proof
epics.objective: Demonstrate that specialization and talent choices change decisions rather than only tooltip numbers.
epics.scope: Two legal builds within one specialization and a contrasting second specialization; bounded talent bindings only.
acceptance_criteria: At least two legal builds in one specialization change at least two recorded decision dimensions across stationary, moving, interrupted, spread-target and short/sustained scenarios while retaining baseline role viability.
A second specialization demonstrates its documented loop and weakness under equal role and equipment budgets.
Positive and exclusion cases cover each enabled behavior-changing talent in the proof package.
Changing the tested builds preserves cooldown, resource, harmful-status and summon restrictions.
epics.completion_evidence: Future build allocations, comparable action traces, human evaluation protocol/results and executed talent fixtures.
epics.ordering_rationale: Prove meaningful branches on a small package before binding all 1,764 nodes. Structurally legal allocation examples are not this evidence.

epics.title: Durable quest objectives and rewards
epics.objective: Track authenticated gameplay objectives and award each completion once.
epics.scope: Quest prerequisites, objective credit, return interactions, tracker and resumable progress; authored starter tasks are BW-039.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted quests advance only on matching successful actor events; duplicate root events clamp to the required count.
Combat credit respects encounter membership and actual damage, healing, prevention, tanking or support participation.
Prerequisite and return requirements reject premature completion; repeated practice never repeats one-time rewards.
Reconnect and full-bag completion retain objective progress and deliver the same awarded assets.
epics.completion_evidence: Future objective-kind fixtures, duplicate-credit tests and persisted completion/reconnect/full-bag demonstrations.

epics.title: Profession enrollment and skill progression
epics.objective: Keep profession learning independent of combat level and talent currencies.
epics.scope: Two manufacturing slots, two gathering slots, three universal life skills, skill 1–300 and deterministic progress accounting. Training and declared acquisition sources grant durable recipe knowledge; deactivation retains learned recipes.
acceptance_criteria: Selection enforces two manufacturing and two gathering slots while Cooking, Fishing and First Aid remain universally available.
Difficulty-relative successful actions award 100/50/20/0 progress units at the documented thresholds and carry remainders.
Cancellation, retries, salvage and material transfers grant no duplicate progress.
Training and band access use authored fees/skill requirements without inventing a character-level gate.

Recipe learning validates its declared acquisition source and eligibility, records unique character/recipe knowledge once across retry/restart, and retains it while the profession is dormant; an unauthorized grant cannot unlock a recipe.
epics.completion_evidence: Future enrollment, progression-threshold and durable retry tests using actual service records.

epics.title: Shared resource nodes and skinning rights
epics.objective: Let eligible players claim bounded resource outputs without duplication or stolen loot reservations.
epics.scope: Mining, Herbalism, Forestry and post-loot Skinning interactions; fishing timing is BW-036.
acceptance_criteria: An ordinary node exposes three charges, a three-second channel and one claim per character per authoritative respawn cycle.
Concurrent completion yields only available charges; a losing or interrupted claim consumes no tools or inputs.
Respawn/replacement follows authored positive timing and active-node caps; clients cannot respawn resources.
Skinning waits for eligible loot resolution/public grace and rejects encounter-reserved carcasses.
epics.completion_evidence: Future contested-node, restart/cycle, interrupted-channel and carcass-reservation scenario results.

epics.title: Quoted synchronous personal crafting
epics.objective: Turn reserved materials into one exact useful output through a recoverable short craft.
epics.scope: A representative band-I manufacturing chain, station validation, result preview and short synchronous jobs; public orders and mastery are separate.
acceptance_criteria: The quote shows exact inputs, deterministic output, recipient, grade, binding, skill progress and required station.
An accepted craft reserves owned versioned inputs; cancellation or precommit failure yields no output or skill.
Commit consumes once, produces once and grants eligible skill once; retries return the existing receipt.
A postcommit crash or full bag preserves the output in durable delivery; disconnected ordinary crafts do not silently become offline jobs.

Unknown or unlearned recipes, insufficient skill, inactive professions and unauthorized stations reject before reservation; legitimate learning makes the same recipe available without bypassing other eligibility rules.
Before the first craft and after recipe/vendor changes, the enabled price/conversion graph passes the shared admission gate; a crafted-output sellback loop is rejected before it can mint value.
epics.completion_evidence: Future real-store concurrency, reservation recovery and pre/postcommit crash tests, plus one usable crafted item demonstration.
epics.ordering_rationale: A small useful craft validates ownership and delivery without requiring marketplace listings or all profession content.

epics.title: Safe local zone transitions and recall
epics.objective: Move a character between declared locations within one authoritative world process without bypassing travel or recovery rules.
epics.scope: Local zone/floor changes, protected destinations, legal return anchors and explicit loading feedback. Cross-process ownership handoff is a separate capability.
acceptance_criteria: Only declared source/destination locations and authorized return anchors can be selected; stale, unknown, cross-instance or inaccessible destinations reject with a specific reason.
Combat, prohibited objectives, locked crafting transactions and unavailable destinations prevent travel under the documented eligibility rules without spending a rejected action cost.
A successful transition presents one destination character and the correct floor/zone visibility; stale source targets and unauthorized interest are removed.
Recall observes its declared cast, cooldown and safe-anchor restrictions; cancellation and failed travel preserve the current authoritative character and committed economic results.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: local transition and recall fixtures covering floors, protected areas, combat/crafting rejection, cancellation, destination failure and stale source messages, plus a demonstrated loading transition.
epics.ordering_rationale: Zone, instance and floor identity must exist with movement; moving between local scopes does not require a fleet or cross-process transfer service.

epics.title: Finite privileged support permissions and audit
epics.objective: Provide traceable support and administrative actions with the documented default-deny realm scopes.
epics.scope: Read-only support, moderation/restrictions, progression/inventory edits, economy freezes/reversals and release/restore authorization. Domain-specific recovery workflows remain separate epics.
acceptance_criteria: Support cannot mutate; moderator, game_master, economy_operator and release_operator can perform only their declared permissions within an explicit authorized realm/target scope.
Missing grants/scopes, unknown permissions, client-supplied roles and attempts to grant unavailable authority reject without side effects.
Every privileged mutation records immutable actor, action identity, target, reason, applicable versions and result; economic changes use canonical receipts/ledgers.
Retried and concurrent grants preserve expected-version and idempotency rules; denied actions cannot create partial inventory, currency or progression edits.
An authorized support user can investigate a character/action using permitted records without seeing credentials, opaque proofs or unnecessary personal data.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: permission/realm matrix tests, unauthorized escalation attempts, duplicate/concurrent edit tests and inspectable redacted audit trails for each allowed mutation family.
epics.ordering_rationale: Manual edits become a second exploit path unless they share ownership and receipt rules. This can be completed on the initial persistent slice before large social/economic systems exist.

epics.title: Economic incident visibility, freezes and reversal
epics.objective: Detect and contain economic corruption while preserving legitimate ownership and a complete audit history.
epics.scope: Receipt/ledger investigation, configured anomaly signals, visible service suspension, scoped asset freezes and authorized fraud reversal. Market balancing and general moderation are separate. Recurring economic reconciliation covers every admitted asset-mutation service.
acceptance_criteria: An authorized investigator traces an item/currency mutation through operation, owner, lineage, content and ledger versions, including duplicate delivery and settlement retry history.

Configured monitoring exposes conservation exceptions, settlement backlog and suspicious repeated mutations with an identified measurement window; no unmeasured profitability or fraud claim is reported.

Configured suspension or asset freeze rejects affected currently enabled economic operations with a user-visible reason while committed outcomes remain reconcilable; later market/crafting services pass the same checks before admission.
A permitted reversal accounts for both items and currency through the canonical transactional path, records its relation to the original operation and cannot selectively rewind one side.
Repeated reversal/freeze requests and concurrent normal operations cannot duplicate assets or conceal the immutable original audit history.

A daily reconciliation report over a declared consistent interval accounts for authorized currency sources/sinks and zero-net internal transfers, identifies unmatched item/receipt/ledger/outbox operations, and exposes missing or failed reconciliation. Every later economic service joins this reconciliation before admission.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: injected duplicate/settlement anomalies, investigation traces, freeze/unfreeze exercises and concurrent idempotent reversal tests against the real database. Later services must join the same incident checks before release. Include executed daily reconciliation with seeded discrepancies, matching interval/checkpoint records and visible failure handling.
epics.ordering_rationale: Containment and conservation can be proven before the bazaar exists; adding a market or guild bank must extend this path instead of creating a new recovery authority.

epics.title: Production identity recovery and security policy
epics.objective: Complete provider-backed authentication, recovery, revocation and explicit endpoint/retention policy for external persistent play.
epics.scope: Trusted adapter integration, transport security, credential/session lifecycle, configured limits, restriction/appeal authorization and bounded retention. Gameplay authority remains with existing domain owners.
acceptance_criteria: The configured trusted provider verifies opaque purpose/account/audience-scoped one-use login/recovery proof; invalid, expired, replayed and wrong-account proofs cannot acquire a character.
Recovery and rotation revoke old handles and owner epochs before fresh control; retries return the stored recovery receipt and cannot authorize another account.
Every published request family has explicit rate, payload and collection limits enforced independently of GCD; missing configuration disables that endpoint.
Account/service traffic uses the chosen standard secure transport, secrets/proofs stay out of logs/public snapshots and configured expiry/retention rules are verified.
Restrictions and appeals preserve original history; only authorized terminal review creates a separate audited action with reviewer/time, and revoked access cannot continue through an old connection.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: chosen-provider integration and adversarial request tests, recovery/revocation races, expiry/retention checks, transport configuration evidence and redacted restriction/appeal audit examples.
epics.ordering_rationale: A trusted test adapter can prove early networking. Real external persistent characters require configured provider security; production values cannot be inferred from the documentation.

epics.title: Consistent backup and verified restore
epics.objective: Restore a recoverable economic checkpoint with reconciled character, item, wallet and receipt ownership.
epics.scope: Versioned backup manifests, artifact integrity, privileged restore, economic consistency and repeatable recovery evidence. Backup-file creation alone is insufficient.
acceptance_criteria: A backup identifies schema/content versions, all artifacts, matching lowercase SHA-256 digests and one economically consistent checkpoint.
A restore rejects missing, corrupt or incompatible artifacts and cannot be marked completed before integrity and required receipt reconciliation pass.
Restoring after committed and pending operations preserves canonical item/wallet ownership and reconciles receipts/outbox; currency cannot be rewound while purchased items remain unaccounted.
Only an authorized scoped release operation performs restore; the audit links backup, action, reconciliation findings and completion time.
An isolated recovery exercise measures the achieved recovery point/time against explicitly approved test objectives and retains blocking findings instead of claiming success from manifest validity.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: an actual real-database restore into an isolated environment, corruption/incompatibility rejection, item/currency/receipt reconciliation and measured recovery results with approved objectives.
epics.ordering_rationale: Require this before persistent external play, including a limited beginner playtest; valuable character state already needs recoverability long before production scale.

epics.title: First complete beginner journey
epics.objective: Deliver the first complete level 1–10 player experience using a declared representative playable roster.
epics.scope: Equivalent faction-separated starter layouts for an initial Warrior/Bard/Mage roster, bound early kits, guidance, solo graduation and a safe explicit exit; full roster acceptance is BW-052.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh supported characters create, enter and complete the five learning stages with abilities at levels 1/3/5/7/9.
Required quests and distinct guaranteed encounter XP reach level 10 before graduation without optional tasks or repeated grinding.

Inventory/equipment, vendor, recovery, an optional party task and optional useful gather/craft practice are accessible within the compact journey; skipping group/profession activities never blocks the required solo path.
Specialization preview spends nine banked points only after confirmation; tank/healer/damage graduation is solo-completable with friendly targets where needed.
Death, shared targets, full bags and logout do not block progress; departure names a valid next objective/destination.

The representative journey uses the selected 3D pixel-art camera and reviewed starter assets; scene occluders, projected targeting and independent UI remain usable, with final environment breadth and full-roster art certified later.
epics.completion_evidence: Future fresh-character end-to-end recordings, required-path XP report, role graduation tests and persisted interruption matrix.
epics.ordering_rationale: A complete beginner experience requires coherent rewards and recovery, but need not wait for all 37 kits, the bazaar, raids or multi-server hosting.

epics.title: Authorized fishing sessions
epics.objective: Resolve fishing catches from a validated interaction instead of a client-selected reward.
epics.scope: Cast timing, eligible output tables, interruption and life-skill progress; authored fishing locations come with world content.
acceptance_criteria: Only an active authorized cast within the authored timing tolerance can resolve its catch table.
A cast resolves once; duplicate catch claims and expired sessions produce no extra item or skill progress.
Invalid timing, interruption and unavailable interaction scopes return explicit failure without consuming unrelated assets.
epics.completion_evidence: Future timing-boundary, replay and full-bag catch tests with authoritative session records.

epics.title: Profession mastery and activation changes
epics.objective: Apply bounded production choices without refill, rounding or switching exploits.
epics.scope: Mastery trees, free idle-station reallocation, dormant learned progress and 24-hour activation cooldown.
acceptance_criteria: One point per ten skill levels reaches 30 points against 45 available ranks, respecting branch prerequisites.
Savings/channel/yield effects stay within 12%/15%/10% caps; rare cores are never saved or duplicated.
Each required input consumes at least one; fractional remainder accounting gives equivalent totals across batch sizes.
Accepted jobs retain their authorized mastery snapshot; switching during active work rejects and deactivation removes active benefits without deleting learned skill.
epics.completion_evidence: Future all-branch allocation tests, batch-equivalence/property tests and active-job switching/restart scenarios.

epics.title: Owned mobile pets and summon commands
epics.objective: Support controlled mobile companions within shared simulation and output budgets.
epics.scope: Summon lifetime/capacity, attack/follow/hold/recall, navigation, owner attribution and command feedback; kit expansion is BW-050.
acceptance_criteria: One four-unit owner capacity/output pool permits one elite or eligible lesser servants, including the resolved two-unit Bonewright exception; atomic replacement never doubles capacity or aggregate output.
Commands reject illegal targets and paths; follow/hold/recall behave visibly without wall crossing.
Death, loss of owner/scope and respecialization remove or reconstruct only the permitted owned summons.
Pet attacks retain root attribution and cannot recursively generate extra rewards or resource budgets.
epics.completion_evidence: Future capacity, blocked-path, ownership-loss and command/state-reconstruction fixtures plus multiplayer demonstration.

epics.title: Bounded static combat deployables
epics.objective: Make traps, totems and linked combat objects behave as finite owned effects.
epics.scope: Placement, trigger, expiry, relocation, owner ceilings and explicit links; portable profession utilities are BW-061.
acceptance_criteria: Totemist uses four total combat totems and at most three links including shared-class objects; relocation cannot preserve duplicate old objects.
Saboteur devices obey the three-active-device policy and each device triggers at most once.
Illegal placement, cross-scope targeting and over-capacity requests reject without free effects or lost committed resources.
Expiry, owner loss, encounter reset and reconstruction preserve the same bounded object/trigger state.
epics.completion_evidence: Future linked-layout, trigger-race, capacity and scope/reconstruction fixture results.

epics.title: Validated combat forms
epics.objective: Change form without duplicating attributes, resources or equipment power.
epics.scope: Druid shared and specialization forms, transition eligibility, role defense, presentation and invalid-action cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Only eligible forms and actions activate; tank health/mitigation requires the valid defensive form.
Form attacks use one normalized equipped-weapon budget and the declared resource pool.
Changing form grants no extra current health, cooldown reset, duplicate aura or resource refill.
Visual state and available actions match the authoritative form after rejection, death and reconnect.
epics.completion_evidence: Future form-transition matrix, budget/resource tests and reconstructed client presentation evidence.

epics.title: Persistent delayed-damage debt
epics.objective: Prove deferred damage remains owed through build and session changes.
epics.scope: Ironbody ledger, bounded delay/clearing, lethal resolution and debt display; ordinary damage transfer already belongs to BW-011.
acceptance_criteria: At most 30% of eligible post-absorb damage is delayed over six seconds, with no second Armor reduction or re-delay.
An authorized Balance spend clears only the declared ledger fraction and cannot treat debt as prevented damage.
Death timing is correct when debt overlaps new damage; disconnect, form/build changes and leaving combat never erase outstanding debt.
The interface displays debt separately from health and shields and resumes the same remaining schedule after recovery.
epics.completion_evidence: Future lethal overlap, respec/disconnect/restart ledger fixtures and matching server/client timelines.
epics.ordering_rationale: Validate a durable timed liability before enabling its tank kit; ordinary health snapshots alone cannot prove debt reconstruction.

epics.title: Periodic effect budget transformations
epics.objective: Allow extension, spreading and consumption without duplicating remaining periodic output.
epics.scope: Disease harvest/acceleration, Burning consumption and healing-seed maturation/consumption; ordinary ticking is BW-014.
acceptance_criteria: Consuming a selected remaining periodic budget removes that source once and cannot preserve future ticks as free output.
Extension/acceleration respects declared total-per-application budgets and fixed baseline tick policies.
Mature healing seeds cannot award both the consumed recovery and a duplicate scheduled tick.
Repeated, expired and immune-target cases preserve caps, owner attribution and resource-generation exclusions.
epics.completion_evidence: Future tick-boundary, simultaneous consume/refresh and repeated-harvest traces with conserved effect budgets.

epics.title: Integrated advanced-mechanic multiplayer probe
epics.objective: Validate interacting state families and their representative network workload before broad kit certification multiplies them.
epics.scope: A bounded local multiplayer integration/workload package using representative summons, static objects, statuses/periodic transforms, forms, songs/signature state and delayed-damage debt. Full-roster balance, cross-process advanced recovery and production capacity remain separate gates.
acceptance_criteria: Independent clients exercise the implemented state families together using a versioned representative package, legal owner/object limits and a declared workload; combined actions preserve effective-result attribution, resource/output caps and outstanding debt.

Late join, interest re-entry, authorization loss and latency/loss/reordering recover coherent authorized current state without duplicate entities/effects or hidden-source disclosure; client feedback agrees with authoritative results.

Repeatable density and join/departure runs retain hardware/configuration, tick percentiles, entity/subscription counts, traffic, queues and memory; legal summon limits and overlapping actionable hazards are represented in the workload. Client captures and frame measurements include real summon/form assets and overlapping telegraphs in the selected render view.

A reviewed report accepts a bounded tested workload and records constraints and follow-up gates before broad kit certification. Unresolved correctness or blocking integration failures prevent completion; these measurements make no production-concurrency promise.
epics.completion_evidence: Executed combined-mechanic multi-client scenarios, impairment and density traces, packet/projection inspection and a reviewed workload/constraint report tied to exact game and content revisions.
epics.ordering_rationale: BW-083 measures the direct-action kernel; isolated family fixtures cannot establish their combined traffic and timing behavior. A small integrated probe retires that risk before cohort expansion while BW-089 and BW-090 retain final recovery and capacity responsibility.

epics.title: Private instance membership and lifecycle
epics.objective: Provide isolated group-owned encounter spaces with controlled admission, departure and reset.
epics.scope: Runtime instance identity, party admission, protected entry/exit, encounter locks and instance cleanup in a single process. Dungeon/raid content and separate-process scheduling remain separate.
acceptance_criteria: Two parties entering the same content receive distinct runtime instances; entities, effects, targeting and chat/interest queries cannot cross the boundary.
Admission checks authoritative membership, capacity, eligibility and encounter state; retries cannot create duplicate occupancy or bypass a lock.
Leaving, disconnecting and rejoining resolve to the configured instance and safe location; an unavailable or closed instance fails safely.
A genuine reset clears encounter-owned hazards, threat, summons and eligibility state without refunding player consumables, resetting cooldown/debt or repeating durable rewards.
Closing an empty or completed instance leaves no orphaned controllable entities or pending ownership claim.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: two-party isolation/admission tests, reconnect and unavailable-instance cases, reset/conservation fixtures and lifecycle diagnostics showing cleanup.
epics.ordering_rationale: Instance isolation is a gameplay/security capability before it is a deployment topology; validate it locally before adding cross-process failure modes.

epics.title: Fenced cross-process character handoff
epics.objective: Transfer a character between two authoritative processes while preserving one owner and committed economic state.
epics.scope: Explicit source suspension, checkpoint, one-use destination proof, epoch claim/revocation and destination snapshot for the currently enabled simple character state. Comprehensive advanced-state certification follows separately.
acceptance_criteria: During handoff new source actions stop; pending economic operations settle or reject before the checkpoint, and committed operations remain durable.
Only the bound destination can consume an unexpired one-use proof for its exact character/checkpoint/epochs; replay, wrong destination and stale epoch reject without spawning another owner.
At every failure boundary one process/epoch retains or recovers authority; the source cannot mutate the character or grant rewards after the destination claim.

Destination state preserves location, current build, long cooldowns and the documented enabled-state checkpoint policy, then reconstructs an owner-private snapshot and independently filtered public view.
Source/destination crash, timeout and disconnect scenarios return the character to a known legal authority/location without duplicating inventory or reversing completed trades.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: two-process fault-injection traces at each handoff boundary, duplicate/expired/wrong-destination proofs, stale-owner reward attempts and inventory/receipt reconciliation across retries.
epics.ordering_rationale: Reserve scope and epoch contracts early, but postpone distributed handoff until local transitions and durable fencing can be observed. One-owner results are required; message delivery is not described as exactly once.

epics.title: Versioned deployment, database migration and rollback
epics.objective: Deploy and replace the small initial service/world deployment without incompatible state or partial economic rollback.
epics.scope: Reproducible release artifacts/configuration, safe admission/drain, database migrations, compatibility checks and rollback/reconciliation. Automatic fleet scaling and independent microservices are not required.
acceptance_criteria: A release identifies the exact client/server artifacts, configuration, content/rules/database versions and supported compatibility; unsupported peers/content reject before mutation.
