open_decisions.title: Engine, platform and deployment candidates
open_decisions.description: Select and pin a tested Unreal Engine 5 revision, native C++ compiler/toolchain, supported platforms, build and dedicated-server targets and Unicode-data revisions. Inventory the owner's available replication plugins and verify each one's license, compatible engine versions, network capabilities and limits before choosing integration; the supplied MultiplayerSessions Steam plugin has baseline compile/widget checks, with actual networking coverage still unverified. The owner-selected game repository now exists; trusted identity, persistence, hosting and deployment remain future work.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-001 demonstrates actual installation, new C++ project and tested build targets; BW-004/BW-013 evaluate builtin replication and compatible owner-provided plugins against connection and disclosure requirements; BW-018/BW-086/BW-088 verify persistence, provider and deployment choices before external play.

open_decisions.title: Capacity, security and recovery budgets
open_decisions.description: Approve concrete per-endpoint lifetimes/limits/retention, expected workload, tick/tail-latency/bandwidth budgets, recovery point/time and release admission envelope. Prototype rates and 20-second grace are starting settings, not established achievements.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before the relevant security/restore/load epic is Complete; final release cannot accept unnamed or unmeasured targets.

open_decisions.title: Concrete world and starter records
open_decisions.description: Author finite functional maps, appearance assets, starter instructions, NPC kits, loot tables, recovery/exit locations and required XP allocations within existing contracts. No names, lore, branching narrative system or detailed new geography are inferred here.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Representative records before BW-039; full-roster starter and level 11–60 content before BW-052/BW-053, and reviewed release-content manifest before BW-092.

open_decisions.title: Runtime bindings and complete release inventory
open_decisions.description: Prototype profiles do not establish the named secondary ability/talent behavior. The supplied 257 recipes and sample items are representative, not the launch inventory. Decide concrete compatible bindings and complete useful content within the documented class/profession scope.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-047–051 and BW-062 certify the intended full scope; BW-092 rejects missing required roster/content rather than silently shrinking the game.

open_decisions.title: Prices, sources and conversion graph
open_decisions.description: Concrete vendor values, recipe conversion values, source distributions, starter XP allocation and economic tuning need authoring and tests. Published fees, six bands and profession relevance targets remain prototype constraints, not measured health.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before enabling the relevant vendor/conversion content; economy/profession measurement in BW-072 and final integration in BW-092.

open_decisions.title: Measured balance, usability and content limits
open_decisions.description: Approve balance deviations and launch content bounds using equal-budget role/build/faction tests, actual progression, supported input devices and accessible visual feedback. Twelve classes, 37 specializations and level cap 60 remain requirements; a smaller technical slice is not permission to omit them.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Representative proof before expansion; BW-071–074 and BW-092 resolve release-blocking findings using documented test standards.

open_decisions.title: Incremental topology and comparable branch orders
open_decisions.description: A small deployment with explicit loading transitions can validate the required game before fleet complexity. Full-state conservative recovery is sufficient under the documented baseline; no exact lost-tick replay, unrestricted rewind or seamless travel requirement is added. Social/profession branches can move earlier if team capacity supports them.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Revisit after BW-083/BW-082 measurements and before BW-090 capacity approval; change ordering while retaining IDs if evidence contradicts the assumption.

open_decisions.title: Concrete item-use timing bindings
open_decisions.description: Authored consumable effect records specify effects, channels and category/recipient restrictions. Any unspecified consumption, interruption/refund and treatment-lock start timing needs an explicit reviewed runtime binding before that item is enabled; do not infer it from animation or let duplicate use choose a favorable policy.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before BW-075 is Complete; preserve published durations, caps, mode exclusions and authoritative conservation.

open_decisions.title: Rated entry eligibility and normalized build selection
open_decisions.description: Rated combat requires effective level 60 and a 118-point budget, but the reference does not specify minimum actual entry level or how a below-cap entrant selects legal normalized talents, role services and ability unlocks. Decide whether entry requires actual level 60 or supports lower-level entrants with an explicitly reviewed temporary build/ability policy. Preserve the required normalization and ordinary earned progression; this audit selects neither alternative.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Approve before BW-067 can be Complete and before BW-068 admits rated participants. Test admitted-level entry/exit/reconnect, temporary mode selections and unchanged ordinary build/progression; do not infer match initialization or respawn policy from ordinary build application.

open_decisions.title: Camera, asset conventions and supported visual quality
open_decisions.description: Pin the tested Unreal Engine version and supported platforms, orthographic starting pitch/framing, third-person camera distance/pitch and projection-transition policy, scroll and middle-mouse orbit sensitivity/limits, aspect/minimum-window policy, model/material/animation conventions, environment presentation and client performance budgets. The camera behaviors are requirements; numerical tuning requires evidence, and no specialized rendering technique is implied.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-097 verifies the camera/readability and display baseline; BW-098 establishes repeatable asset conventions; BW-099 reviews complete environments; BW-074/BW-090 approve release visual accessibility and performance across supported quality tiers.

deferred_scope: Neutral/cross-faction exchanges, war logistics, timed auctions and financial instruments are outside the baseline economy; neither faction depends on enemy supply. Faction-local fixed-price listings and buyer requests remain required.
Race/faction transfers and class changes are not launch capabilities. Optional cosmetic account collections grant no account-wide combat power or profession throughput.

Housing, territory, sieges, authored geography/lore and long offline manufacturing are outside the current documented baseline. This roadmap requires functional maps/assets/content, without inventing worldbuilding.

Voice chat and seamless travel are optional, not prerequisites. Explicit transitions and a small deployment satisfy the initial topology; larger raid sizes and fleet growth require authored limits and measurements.
No required catalog family is silently deferred beyond the full-game gate. Incomplete bespoke content remains disabled during earlier slices and must be bound/certified for the intended full roster.
critical_review: Moved the durable ownership/recovery probe into the first review group so database correctness can be tested alongside simulation instead of waiting for a full role encounter. It has no combat dependency.

Kept privacy in the initial entity projection and added richer relevance bounds before the first integrated action. Prediction follows authoritative movement but is a recommendation for the technical proof, not a fabricated prerequisite of numerical combat.

Introduced a representative signature-resource probe before role and starter integration; full pets, forms, maintained support and damage-debt families precede roster expansion, rather than every first playable interaction.

Separated a representative beginner playtest from full-roster level 1–10 certification. Optional crafting and grouping remain optional to a player, while the documented introductions still need integration evidence.

Separated local travel and instance identity from cross-process ownership. Simple handoff is tested before final advanced-state recovery; the first handoff does not certify mechanics introduced afterward.

Removed global phase barriers and kept social, profession and economic branches independently actionable. Recommended predecessors express integration convenience; only observable prerequisites are hard edges.

Required provider security and a real restore before persistent external testing, while early headless fixtures and restricted technical sessions stay small. Final capacity and incidents wait for representative full workloads.

Retained separate full-game integration and release gates. Completion percentages describe epic counts only; undefined capacity, balance targets or launch-content bounds cannot be replaced by optimistic status updates.

A competent team could move some profession/social work earlier or defer a simple handoff until larger zones exist. This order favors earlier conservation/ownership learning; it makes no claim that those comparable branch orders have a unique optimum.

Independent audit: retain the initial network/replication order, add explicit content production and a combined-family probe, enforce only demonstrated hard prerequisites, and leave rated entry/build selection as an explicit unresolved policy. See the Roadmap Audit for baseline evidence and per-epic dispositions.

Art-direction revision: replaced the former 2D sprite mandate with the selected 3D pixel-art reference. BW-097/BW-098/BW-099 cover early orthographic camera/readability verification, reusable art production and environment integration, while independent headless development and full release visual/performance checks remain required.
maintenance: Edit only sources/development-roadmap.json for planning, status and evidence; preserve stable IDs, AC anchors, dependencies and authoritative contracts. Generated progress/readiness views derive from it.

Use Not Started, In Progress, Blocked or Complete. Implemented work awaiting human acceptance stays In Progress with the exact gap recorded; a PR can be delivered before acceptance. Blocked needs a real prerequisite. Planning alone starts or completes no work.

Complete requires executed passing evidence for every AC and complete dependencies. Evidence records use criteria, artifact, revision, result and summary; result may be Passed, Failed or Not Run. Not Run — Manual QA Pending is never a pass. Preserve accepted history; reopen completion only when current evidence is invalidated.

Before decomposition, read the parent ACs, relevant contracts/dependencies and current implementation owners once. Reuse existing game/Unreal/plugin functionality; API presence does not prove integration. Record only findings that change the ticket plan, without a separate capability-audit framework.

Each ticket defines a small outcome, owner, scope/exclusions, dependencies, exact epic_criteria coverage and appropriate verification. Together tickets cover every parent AC. Prefer deterministic unit tests, affected C++ compilation/native tests and concise human QA; preserve authority, invalid-input rejection, privacy and actual integration requirements.

Follow docs/validation.md for workflow scope, generation, evidence and the protected verification budget. Routine ticket changes use one roadmap generation command and focused gate, no inventory review refresh, browser, Unreal run, ancestor audit or duplicate report tree. Update parent completion only when its own criteria actually qualify.

For human QA provide prerequisites/map/controls, steps, expected/failure behavior and cleanup; record actual execution separately. Codex need not automate it. Quantitative requirements still need suitable objective evidence. No default GIF/frame/capture framework or multi-configuration matrix.

Keep one concise result summary or durable PR link when evidence is needed. Retain historical public acceptance links, not new log/capture archives. Increasing routine scope/budgets requires an explicitly authorized workflow change with defect, cheaper-alternative analysis and recurring cost.

tickets.title: Record attributable executed fixture evidence
scope: Reuse the completed BW-001/BW-002 owners: tools/check_baseline.py for toolchain/source identity and bounded process handling; FContentContracts/FValidationFinding/FContentRevisions/FContentAdmission for canonical validation, compatible revisions and atomic selection; ContentAdmissionTestSupport and FContentCompatibilityRun for existing native test/report behavior. Add only the missing fixture evidence adapter, native automation cases under Source/Briarwake/Tests and tools/check_runtime_fixtures.py. Keep the existing seven tests and their exact assertion/report checks intact, using Unreal Automation and the existing WITH_EDITOR && WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS boundary. Exclude fixture code, inputs and controls from normal Game/Server packages.

Select a small immutable positive/negative corpus from fixtures/content_admission/admission.json, preserving its fixture IDs, ContentValidationFixture specifications, package inputs, exact content/rules revisions and expected ValidationFinding values. Execute the real FContentAdmission boundary rather than copying admission rules or claiming that existing admission evidence already implements BW-003. Reuse ContentValidationResult for actual admission findings and expectation matching. Keep authored run_evidence unexecuted; store actual FixtureRunEvidence separately with runner, UTC time and matching revisions. A correctly rejected candidate can yield a passed test with nonempty ContentValidationResult.actual_findings and empty FixtureRunEvidence.findings; reserve failed execution evidence findings for test failures. Attach actual TestCheck assertions and engine/build/source/fixture identities in a test evidence envelope; ValidationReport remains the documentation report and is not a partial runtime envelope.

Provide the transient UWorld lifecycle, bounded immutable fixture selection, execution/report adapter and documented native build/launch/reset steps. Reuse tools/extract_content_contracts.py and FContentContracts for canonical TestCheck extraction if needed, preserving existing definitions and fingerprints rather than copying a schema into the runner. Distinguish build/load/startup failure, missing execution/report and executed assertion failure. Implement assertion-failure, missing-report, load-failure, startup-failure and timeout controls; require the expected stage-specific evidence so an unavailable engine cannot satisfy a control. Reject stale/foreign identities, duplicate/missing assertions and reused output directories. Integrate the evidence suite into tools/validate.py without weakening prerequisite gates.
out_of_scope: Combat/ability execution, player connectivity, persistence, production telemetry and a generic fixture scripting language.
Treating authored expectations, a documentation schema check or an old Godot run as current Unreal execution evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Native execution through FContentAdmission preserves exact existing fixture IDs/encodings and immutable specifications. Actual acceptance/rejection and ContentValidationResult.actual_findings match expectations; a correctly rejected candidate records a passed FixtureRunEvidence with no blocking findings, while a deliberately wrong expectation records an executed failed assertion and failed run evidence with findings.

Unexecuted specifications retain status unexecuted, null runner_id/completed_at and empty execution findings. Separate passed/failed evidence requires an actual runner, valid UTC completion time, matching tested content/rules revisions and canonical finding constraints. Unknown scenario encodings, missing required fields, stale/mismatched identities and duplicate/missing assertion records are rejected. Runtime envelopes do not masquerade as incomplete ValidationReport objects.

Clean execution produces complete attributable records and returns success only after actual assertion/report verification. Each failure control and a child timeout returns nonzero with the correct stage; none fabricates a gameplay pass or changes immutable specifications.
tickets.completion_evidence: Retain native build/test commands, toolchain identity, fixture/source hashes, passing admission execution, failing controls, timeout cleanup and clean recovery. Map artifacts to ticket ACs; documentation checks alone are not this evidence.

scope: Extend the T01 transient-world/native automation owner with FRuntimeFixtureContext, a finite local diagnostic action probe with controlled fixture clock, deterministic random stream and bounded pending effects. Support the named transient empty-world configuration; reject unsupported populated worlds/configurations explicitly. Reuse FContentContracts rather than a second validator. Keep local probe steps typed and test-owned, use canonical TestCheck for probe assertions and preserve existing FixtureStep/FixtureAssertion variants.

Commit finite scenarios for accepted/rejected probe input, bounded queued execution, same-context replay, explicit seed/context change and reset. Reject invalid/nonfinite/out-of-order timing and unsupported controls before mutation. Expose context reset/seed/clock controls only to compiled automation code; exclude them from gameplay RPCs, console/Exec/Blueprint commands and packaged launch options. Add normal client/server negative-launch checks and a documented context suite.

Reuse assessment 2026-10-22: extend the verified T01 FRuntimeFixtureEvidence, transient UWorld lifecycle, stage attribution and canonical reader. The local probe adds only deterministic context/queued decision state; it must not recreate MultiplayerSessions, native movement/prediction or a production command dispatcher. See the dated capability review on roadmap-maintenance.html.
out_of_scope: Creating the future world, session, ability or combat systems to run a diagnostic experiment.
Client-selectable seeds/time/owner epochs, arbitrary property-path mutation, production cheats or a new gameplay command protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Two fresh runs of identical context and ordered inputs reproduce accepted/rejected results, committed probe-effect counts and ordering. Wall-clock timings/run IDs may differ and are excluded from rule equality. Changing the declared seed/context is attributable and a reset reproduces the original outcome.

The canonical reader accepts the supported empty-world FixtureWorldContext without changing its field meanings: zero ticks/epochs are valid and seeds remain opaque nonempty strings. Missing/unknown fields, null required collections, negative counters, invalid UTC timestamps, wrong seed types, nonfinite timing, decreasing offsets and unsupported controls fail before mutation. Re-extraction preserves all previously supported canonical definitions and compatibility cases.

Normal client/server artifacts contain no usable test control path. Attempts to set test seeds, reset state or advance time through ordinary gameplay/launch surfaces fail without mutation; absence of a production RPC dispatcher is recorded rather than claimed as a network attack test.

scope: Extend the existing admission owner with an economic graph check only after T05 resolves and publishes its canonical inputs. Cover the complete requested enabled vendor purchase/sellback, crafting, material conversion and salvage graph, including paths crossing several records and already enabled dependencies; do not certify each recipe independently.

Use explicit guaranteed costs/quantities and currency minor units with checked arithmetic. Honor crafted sellback strictly below guaranteed NPC-purchased input cost, material loss on craft/salvage, at most 25% eligible common returns, zero rare/bound component return and zero salvage gold/XP. Distinguish guaranteed repeatable paths from random output or finite supplies; missing price/mapping/provenance/required quantity prevents affected route activation. No inferred market-price oracle or default zero.

If the analyzer cannot prove the gate for a supported request, return an actionable finding and keep the candidate disabled; a search timeout or partial traversal never certifies safety. tickets.title: Enforce concurrent revision, retry and ownership-epoch checks
scope: Keep all mutation authorization, optimistic version comparisons, scoped operation-key uniqueness and ownership-epoch fencing inside the same native SQLite transaction owner from T02. Use durable conditional updates/constraints rather than only an in-process mutex or a preflight SELECT. Serialize requests through the database across independent connections; classify a bounded SQLITE_BUSY/lock outcome explicitly and never treat it as an accepted mutation.

Scope idempotency to the authenticated actor and operation. Persist a canonical identity of the validated semantic request with the terminal receipt; exact retry returns the original receipt/result without revalidating already-consumed expected versions as a new mutation. Reusing that key with changed item, destination, amount or other operation semantics rejects without altering the original receipt. Identical key text in another actor/operation scope cannot read or reuse a private receipt. Receipt lookup/replay does not itself authorize a new economic write.

Persist SessionOwnershipRecord/SessionAuthority compare-and-claim state. Check the caller’s trusted process/epoch against the current row at mutation commit, fencing stale writers after claim/revocation. Only one claimant may advance a given epoch; stale, reused, wrapped or unrepresentable epochs/revisions reject without new asset effects. This storage fence does not implement login, session proofs or zone transfer. Existing FRuntimeFixtureContext foreign-epoch/AcceptedActions checks are test-memory behavior and must not be used as durability evidence.

Use a bounded real race with independently opened SQLite connections and a barrier at the conflicting write, not sequential calls labeled concurrent. Cover competing stale-revision mutations, simultaneous identical retries, conflicting key reuse and a claim-versus-stale-writer interleaving. Verify persisted rows/receipt/ledger/outbox counts after both participants finish and after reopen. Add pure/unit cases only for distinct request-identity/range rejection responsibilities, through the actual owner.
out_of_scope: Steam or network admission, authentication providers, distributed leases, multi-shard consensus, production session lifecycle, respec/combat authority and load/capacity benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent conflicting requests with the same expected asset revisions commit at most one mutation; the loser receives explicit stale/lock findings and persisted assets, ledger and outbox remain conserved. A bounded lock wait cannot silently succeed or hang the runner.

Exact sequential, simultaneous and post-reopen retries return the recorded receipt and result with no second debit, item move, revision advance or outbox entry. Changed semantic payload under the same scoped key rejects; another actor/operation scope gains no access to that result.

After a durable ownership claim advances the epoch, a stale process/epoch cannot commit any new asset change, even if it passed earlier validation. A real claim/write race produces a serializable valid outcome with one current authority; epoch/revision exhaustion cannot wrap or reuse a fence.
tickets.completion_evidence: Actual independent-connection races and persisted conservation/receipt/epoch assertions against the selected SQLite file, plus focused request-identity/range checks and affected compilation. Record participants and ordering; a Python fake or sequential-only test is not concurrency evidence.

Record actual TransactionRecoveryTestRecord findings/conservation fields and a short revision/phase/receipt summary using existing evidence ownership. Keep crash switches and fixture seeds behind existing Editor/development guards, unreachable through gameplay commands; child nonzero exit alone or a missing report is not a successful crash test. acceptance_criteria: Actual abrupt child termination before commit leaves the prior complete economic state; termination after durable commit before acknowledgment preserves the complete mutation and exact original receipt. Fresh-process retry never duplicates, loses or partially restores its item/currency changes.

Failures before delivery and after durable recipient acceptance but before producer delivered marking recover from the same pending outbox. Redelivery is harmless and produces one durable recipient effect with the original notification identity; no item/wallet/ledger mutation runs again.

Each claimed crash result proves its reached phase and fresh-process database assertions with conserved items/currency and one owner.
